description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.notes: Schema, bus, episodic memory, agent base. Nothing alive yet — just the substrate everything else hangs off.

phases.title: First Voice
phases.notes: Cheshire Cat end-to-end. Talking to himself. Layered context composer + engagement policy + ADR writer come online here because the Cat is their first consumer.

phases.title: First Tension
phases.notes: Add the White Rabbit. Two voices, role tension, semantic + relational memory layers populated as the agents accumulate history. Compaction-as-behavior arrives because it has to.

phases.title: First Race
phases.notes: Dodo orchestrator + quiescence + conflict resolution + first showcase (/health endpoint). The system runs end-to-end on a trivial directive. Init CLI lands here so the showcase can run against a real target project.

phases.title: Full Cast
phases.notes: Bring the rest of the cast online with integration tests per agent. Per-character artifact handlers for the new speech act payloads. Synthetic-consensus guard goes here because it only matters once disagreement is real.

phases.title: Real Threads
phases.notes: The hard showcases — translation chat MVP, security recovery, multi-session persistence. Transcript annotation tooling lets us publish them. Token telemetry confirms the engagement_policy is paying for itself. Closed out 2026-05-08; substrate-convergence work in analyses 026-030 + the Geocities showcase landed the "Tweedles don't ship" bug class. P7 evals deferred behind P8 (operator interface) so the eval harness has a usable surface to run against.

phases.title: Observer API
phases.notes: HistoricalRunHandle reads any captured snapshot directory — parses run.log, reads the per-agent SQLite databases, loads the telemetry JSON, exposes summary() / meetings() / utterances() / per_agent_telemetry() / artifacts(). The replay-side surface that everything else in P8 sits on. Shipped 2026-05-07 alongside P8.2.

phases.title: TUI Inspector
phases.notes: Textual-based read-only TUI: snapshot library, run summary, meeting detail with body preview + speaker filter + utterance modal, artifact browser (global + meeting-scoped, attribution via bus not mtime), cast view, theme cycling, app-wide vim navigation. First public release — wonderland-ai 0.0.1 on PyPI 2026-05-08.

phases.title: Streaming + Mock Turtle
phases.notes: Foundation for live-watch UX. Extend RunHandle with stream_events() async iterator; HistoricalRunHandle defaults to yield-now (no behavior change for inspector); MockTurtleHandle replays a snapshot's events with compressed timing + dwell cap so we iterate live-watch UI against a free testbed. After P8.3 the TUI can subscribe to "events as they arrive" without caring whether the source is replay, mock, or eventually a real bus.

phases.title: Live-watch screen
phases.notes: New LiveRunScreen that consumes the streaming API — meeting cells fill in as events arrive, current speaker indicator, live cost ticker, drill-down into in-progress meetings shows partial transcripts. Iterated entirely against Mock Turtle replay so zero API spend during UX iteration. The screen that turns Wonderland from "things happen and you read transcripts later" into "things happen and you watch them happen."

phases.title: Directive issuing + LiveRunHandle
phases.notes: NewRunScreen — directive textarea, workflow picker (TDD/canonical/smoke), project-root picker. LiveRunHandle wraps a real Runner+Caucus, emits via the same streaming API as MockTurtleHandle so the live-watch screen consumes both interchangeably. The leap from "replay testbed" to "actually launches a real run." First end-to-end test: directive → live watch → artifacts → done.

phases.title: New-project spinup (the rabbit hole)
phases.notes: Three entry paths converging on a single project-context capture: greenfield (skeleton picker + scaffold), existing-Wonderland (already covered by P8.5's project picker), adopt-existing (wonderland init + stack-detection routine that pre-fills the context form from manifest files). Persists .wonderland/project-context.md in a forward-compatible shape so future workflow-context injection has one input format to read. The on-ramp that turns "pip install" into "team's ready to start."

phases.title: First-use polish
phases.notes: Welcome/home screen (new run / browse snapshots / cast / configure), error states (missing API key, no project root, run failure), abort flow (clean shutdown of running threads), quiescence indicator (M5's long pauses need "still working, just thinking"), README + SHOWCASE updates with the TUI flow. The rough-edges sweep that closes the gap between "works for the developer" and "works for someone who just installed it."

phases.title: Evals
phases.notes: Generic-baseline vs Wonderland comparison. The compounding-curve plot is the legibility-of-value mitigation from §11. Without this the philosophy stays assertion.

activePhase.title: Directive issuing + LiveRunHandle
activePhase.goal: Issue directives + watch live runs from inside the TUI. Two halves merge here: a NewRunScreen for composing the directive (with preset support — bundled in closet/directives/ + per-project saved at <project>/.wonderland/directives/), and a LiveRunHandle that wraps a real Runner+Caucus and emits through the same streaming API the MockTurtleHandle uses, so P8.4's live-watch screen consumes both interchangeably without UI branching. Acceptance: type a directive (or pick a preset) → hit Go → watch the team work end-to-end on the live-watch screen → real production code lands on disk → run completes inside the TUI without dropping to a CLI. Post-P8.5 is when we cut the next PyPI release ('wonderland-ai' bumps to 0.1.0 since this is the first cut anyone outside can pip install + immediately do real work with).
activePhase.sequencing: Directive preset substrate first (T50) so the NewRunScreen has the data model to pick from when it lands. Then the UI shell (T51) — layout-only, with hand-built preset list, before the launch behavior is wired. Then LiveRunHandle (T52) — the substrate that translates RunnerEvent → RunEvent so the live-watch screen sees the same shape from a real run as from MockTurtle. Then the wire-up (T53) — Go button kicks off Runner + workflow + LiveRunHandle and pushes LiveRunScreen against it; first end-to-end test lives here as the acceptance. T54 closes the preset loop with save-as-preset persisting to .wonderland/directives/, completing the per-project story. Per the project_tui_lazygit_principle memory: NewRunScreen layout is multi-pane (preset picker + composer + workflow/skeleton picker), focusable Tab cycle, no modals except for irreversible actions (the launch confirmation, since burning $3-5 should require deliberate consent).

tasks.title: Directive preset module + bundled directives
tasks.details:
The data substrate for preset directives. Composes with closet's existing skeleton + workflow patterns.

Schema (src/wonderland/directive.py, mirrored on workflow.py / skeleton conventions):

  DirectivePreset:
    name: str (e.g. 'pomodoro', 'hello-endpoint')
    title: str (human-readable, e.g. 'Build a Pomodoro timer app')
    description: str (a paragraph explaining what this directive
      asks for — shown as a hover/preview when the user picks
      from the preset list)
    body: str (the actual directive text fed to the runner;
      multi-line)
    suggested_workflow: str | None (e.g. 'tdd-serial' — UI may
      pre-select but never lock)
    suggested_skeleton: str | None (e.g.
      'fullstack-fastapi-react')
    tags: list[str] (e.g. ['greenfield', 'feature-rich'])

Loader functions:
  - list_directives() → bundled names from closet/directives/
  - load_directive(name) → DirectivePreset
  - list_project_directives(project_root) → per-project presets
    from project_root/.wonderland/directives/
  - save_directive(preset, project_root) → write YAML to
    project_root/.wonderland/directives/<slug>.yaml. Used by
    T54's save-as-preset.

Bundle (src/wonderland/closet/directives/):
  - pomodoro.yaml — 'Build a Pomodoro timer app: focus sessions,
    configurable breaks, daily review, persistent settings.'
  - hello-endpoint.yaml — 'Build a /hello endpoint that returns
    the current server time as JSON.'
  - translation-chat.yaml — Showcase 2 directive
  - geocities.yaml — Showcase 5 directive (the SHOWCASE.md run)
  - ping.yaml — for the smoke workflow

Tests (tests/test_directive.py):
  - schema accepts a minimal preset (name, title, body)
  - loader finds bundled presets by name
  - load_directive raises FileNotFoundError with available list
    on miss
  - per-project loader handles missing .wonderland/directives/
    gracefully (returns [])
  - save_directive writes a parseable YAML

Acceptance: list_directives() returns ≥4 bundled names; load_directive('pomodoro').body matches the directive analyses 029-032 used.
tasks.resolution:
T50 ships the directive preset substrate.

Module: src/wonderland/directive.py with DirectivePreset (Pydantic) + loader/saver functions. Schema mirrors the workflow + skeleton patterns: name (slug), title (display), description (paragraph), body (the actual directive text), suggested_workflow (hint), suggested_skeleton (hint), tags (list).

Loader API:
  - directives_dir() / project_directives_dir(project_root) for path resolution
  - list_directives() / list_project_directives(project_root) for discovery
  - load_directive(name_or_path) for bundled presets (with helpful error message listing available presets on miss)
  - load_project_directive(name, project_root) for per-project presets
  - save_directive(preset, project_root) creates .wonderland/directives/ if missing, writes a human-readable YAML preserving field order

Bundled presets (src/wonderland/closet/directives/):
  - pomodoro.yaml — analyses 029-032 substrate-convergence directive (tdd-serial)
  - hello-endpoint.yaml — smoke-level endpoint test (smoke workflow)
  - translation-chat.yaml — Showcase 2 directive (tdd-serial, GDPR-aware)
  - geocities.yaml — SHOWCASE.md banner directive (tdd-serial, multi-tenant)
  - ping.yaml — cheapest possible sanity directive (smoke)

Tests (tests/test_directive.py, 17 cases):
  - Schema: minimal preset, full preset, required fields enforced
  - Bundled: directories resolve, list returns canonical set, pomodoro body matches the analyses-cited directive, by-name vs by-path equivalence, missing raises with available list
  - Per-project: missing dir → [], save creates dir + round-trips, list reflects saves, missing project preset raises, saved YAML is human-readable (field order preserved, multi-line body in literal block style)
  - Sanity: every bundled preset loads cleanly + every suggested_workflow points at an actual bundled workflow (catches typos before they ship)

1368 tests pass full suite.

T51 next: NewRunScreen layout — preset picker + directive composer + workflow/skeleton selectors. The data substrate is ready; the UI shell can pick from it.

tasks.title: NewRunScreen layout — preset picker, directive composer, workflow/skeleton selectors
tasks.details:
The UI shell for kicking off a run. T51 ships layout + state-only against hand-built data; T53 wires the Go button.

Layout (lazygit-style multi-pane per project memory):

  ┌─ New run ───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ [b]Compose a directive[/b] · pick preset or write fresh  │
  ├─ Presets ──────────────┬─ Directive ─────────────────────┤
  │ ▶ pomodoro              │ Build a Pomodoro timer app:    │
  │   hello-endpoint        │ focus sessions, configurable   │
  │   translation-chat      │ breaks, daily review,          │
  │   geocities             │ persistent settings.           │
  │   ping                  │                                │
  │   ───────────────       │                                │
  │   (project presets)     │                                │
  │   custom-feature-X      │                                │
  │                         │                                │
  ├─ Configuration ─────────┴────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Workflow: tdd-serial ▾    Project: /home/jaryk/foo       │
  │ Budget:   \$5.00           Speed: 1x (real-time)         │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  [ Go (g) · Save as preset (s) · Cancel (esc) ]

Behavior:
  - Selecting a preset on the left fills the directive composer
    and pre-selects the suggested_workflow / suggested_skeleton
  - Directive composer is a TextArea — preset picks are starting
    points, never locks
  - Workflow + project-root + budget are dropdown / input widgets
  - 'g' (or Enter on the Go button) triggers launch — wired
    in T53
  - 's' opens the save-as-preset modal (T54)
  - 'escape' returns to wherever the user came from (typically
    snapshot library)

Implementation:
  - src/wonderland/tui/screens/new_run.py with NewRunScreen
  - Reactive properties: selected_preset_name, directive_text,
    workflow_name, project_root, budget
  - When selected_preset_name changes, populate the composer
  - When the user types in the composer, mark selected_preset_name
    as 'custom (modified)' so saving offers to write a new preset
  - Preset list assembled from list_directives() + list_project_directives()

Wire from snapshot library: 'n' (new run) opens NewRunScreen.

Tests (in tests/test_tui_smoke.py):
  - mounts cleanly without a project root
  - preset selection populates the composer
  - editing the composer marks it modified
  - workflow picker exposes all bundled workflows
  - 'g' binding triggers the action method (T51 stub; T53 fills in)

Acceptance: screen mounts + renders; preset picker drives the composer; 'g' triggers a launch action method (no-op stub for now).
tasks.resolution:
T51 ships the NewRunScreen layout.

Three regions per the lazygit principle:

  - Preset picker (left, 38%): DataTable showing bundled directives + per-project directives below a divider when present. Cursor selection populates the composer + pre-selects the suggested workflow.
  - Directive composer (right, 1fr): Static description line + TextArea for the actual directive body.
  - Configuration row (bottom): Workflow Select dropdown (lists all bundled workflows), Budget Input ('$5.00' default), Project root Input (defaults to cwd).

Bindings:
  - 'g' or Enter on the Go button → action_go (validates inputs, notifies; T53 wires the actual Runner launch)
  - 's' → action_save_as_preset (T54 stub)
  - 'escape' → back to caller

Wired entry: 'n' on SnapshotLibraryScreen pushes NewRunScreen. Footer shows the binding.

Selection-driven population: when the cursor moves to a preset row, the description Static updates with the preset's description, the TextArea fills with the preset's body, and the workflow Select pre-selects the suggested_workflow. User is free to edit afterwards — presets are starting points, not locks.

Validation in action_go: empty directive, missing workflow, empty project, non-positive budget all surface as notifications rather than crashing. T53 builds the actual Runner launch on top of the validated inputs.

Tests (+4 in tests/test_tui_smoke.py):
  - mounts cleanly + populates ≥5 bundled presets
  - 'n' from snapshot library opens it
  - cursor on pomodoro row populates composer with 'Pomodoro... focus sessions...' + sets workflow to 'tdd-serial'
  - action_go on empty inputs notifies, doesn't crash

46 TUI smoke tests pass total.

Bug caught + fixed: initial implementation passed Select(value=Select.BLANK) which Textual rejects (interprets as value=False). Removed; Select with allow_blank=True starts blank by default.

T52 next: LiveRunHandle — the substrate that wraps a real Runner+Caucus and translates RunnerEvent → RunEvent so P8.4's LiveRunScreen consumes a live run interchangeably with MockTurtleHandle.

tasks.title: LiveRunHandle — wrap Runner+Caucus, translate RunnerEvent → RunEvent
tasks.details:
The substrate that lets P8.4's LiveRunScreen consume a real run interchangeably with MockTurtleHandle.

Implementation (src/wonderland/observer/live.py):

  class LiveRunHandle(RunHandle):
      def __init__(self, runner, workflow, directive):
          ...

      async def stream_events(self) -> AsyncIterator[RunEvent]:
          # Drive run_workflow internally; translate each
          # RunnerEvent / MeetingStartEvent / MeetingEndEvent
          # produced by run_workflow() into our RunEvent shape.
          ...

      def summary(self) -> RunSummary:
          # Snapshot the runner's current accumulated state.
          ...

      def meetings(self) -> list[RunMeeting]:
          ...

      # etc.

Translation layer:
  - run_workflow yields MeetingStartEvent + MeetingEndEvent + RunnerEvent (kind=utterance/complete/timeout/budget). Each becomes our P8.3 RunEvent shape.
  - RunnerEvent(kind='utterance', payload={'utterance': u}) → UtteranceEmitted(timestamp=u.timestamp, utterance=u). Plus ArtifactShipped emissions for each disk-resolvable utterance.content.artifacts.
  - run_workflow's MeetingStartEvent → MeetingStarted with iteration_index/total/label populated when present (workflow.py already carries these).
  - run_workflow's MeetingEndEvent → MeetingEnded with cost_delta / calls_delta / outcome populated.
  - RunStarted fires before the workflow loop; RunEnded after.
  - AgentTelemetryDelta could fire periodically (every N events) so the live cost ticker climbs smoothly. Or once at the end like Historical does. Start with end-of-stream; iterate later if needed.

Setup ergonomics:
  - LiveRunHandle owns the runner lifecycle (runner.setup + run_workflow + runner.teardown). Caller passes runner config; handle handles cleanup on cancellation.
  - Cancellation: if the user aborts mid-stream (TUI screen pops, or 'a' for abort), the @work-decorated consumer in LiveRunScreen cancels the worker; LiveRunHandle's finally block calls runner.teardown to avoid leaving threads dangling.

Tests (tests/test_observer_live.py):
  - Construct against a Runner mocked to yield a known RunnerEvent sequence; verify the events come out in the right order with the right shapes.
  - Cleanup verified: simulate cancellation; runner.teardown called.

Acceptance: a polymorphic consumer (e.g. test_polymorphic_consumer pattern from test_mock_turtle.py) iterates LiveRunHandle and HistoricalRunHandle interchangeably, getting the same event shape.
tasks.resolution:
T52 ships LiveRunHandle.

Module: src/wonderland/observer/live.py with LiveRunHandle implementing the abstract RunHandle interface. Wraps a real Runner+Workflow+directive and translates RunnerEvent + workflow's MeetingStartEvent/MeetingEndEvent into the P8.3 RunEvent shape so LiveRunScreen consumes it interchangeably with HistoricalRunHandle / MockTurtleHandle.

Lifecycle (in stream_events):
  1. await runner.setup()
  2. yield RunStarted with the run summary
  3. async-for on run_workflow(...) — translate each emitted event:
     - workflow.MeetingStartEvent → MeetingStarted (carries thread_id + iteration metadata)
     - RunnerEvent(kind='utterance') → UtteranceEmitted + ArtifactShipped events for each utterance.content.artifacts that resolves to a path
     - workflow.MeetingEndEvent → MeetingEnded (cost_delta / calls_delta / outcome from the workflow event itself, populated from runner accumulation)
     - RunnerEvent(kind='budget_exceeded'/'timeout'/'aborted') → tracked as final outcome, surfaces in RunEnded
     - state / consensus_alert / telemetry / budget_warning / escalation_prompt / complete: not translated for streaming consumers in v1
  4. yield AgentTelemetryDelta per agent (final from runner.telemetry.per_agent)
  5. yield RunEnded with final summary
  6. finally: await runner.teardown() — even on cancellation, so background threads don't leak when the LiveRunScreen worker is cancelled mid-stream

Non-streaming methods (summary, meetings, utterances, artifacts, per_agent_telemetry) snapshot accumulated state at call time. Mid-stream callers see the in-progress run; post-stream callers see the completed state. Meetings list updates in place via dataclasses.replace as MeetingEnded events arrive (frozen=True dataclass; can't mutate, can replace).

Tests (tests/test_observer_live.py, 11 cases):
  - Lifecycle (3): setup called at stream start; teardown called on completion AND on cancellation (consumer aborts mid-stream)
  - Event translation (5): RunStarted first / RunEnded last; meeting starts and ends balance; utterance → UtteranceEmitted; attached artifact → ArtifactShipped; per-agent telemetry deltas at end with one entry per emitting agent
  - Non-streaming methods (2): summary after run reflects workflow_name / directive / project_root / outcome; meetings() returns completed RunMeeting records with terminal outcomes
  - Polymorphic consumer (1): function typed against abstract RunHandle iterates LiveRunHandle the same way it iterates HistoricalRunHandle / MockTurtleHandle (the acceptance criterion for the phase)

All exercised against a fake Runner so no API tokens burned. The Workflow → run_workflow wiring is real; only the agent-execution layer is stubbed.

1387 tests pass full suite.

Re-exported from wonderland.observer alongside HistoricalRunHandle and MockTurtleHandle.

T53 next: wire NewRunScreen's Go button to construct Runner.make_full_cast → wrap in LiveRunHandle → push LiveRunScreen against it. First end-to-end ('directive → live watch → artifacts → done' from inside the TUI).

tasks.title: Wire NewRunScreen Go → live launch + LiveRunScreen handoff (first end-to-end)
tasks.details:
The leap from 'two screens that don't talk' to 'directive → live run end-to-end inside the TUI'.

Implementation:
  - NewRunScreen.action_go: validate inputs (directive non-empty, workflow loadable, project root exists), construct Runner.make_full_cast(project_root, budget), construct LiveRunHandle wrapping it + the workflow + the directive, push LiveRunScreen with the handle.
  - LiveRunScreen constructor extended to accept a RunHandle directly (in addition to the existing snapshot_dir path). The screen uses the handle's stream_events and non-streaming methods identically; no UI code changes from P8.4.

Confirmation step:
  - Before launching, push a small modal showing 'About to launch: <directive preview>, workflow <name>, budget \$X. Continue?' with Yes / No buttons. Burning \$3-5 should require deliberate consent. Especially important since reading the budget cap from the workflow YAML defaults often gives surprisingly-large numbers (tdd-serial defaults to \$5).

API key resolution:
  - Same chain the runner already uses (env var → config file). NewRunScreen surfaces a clear error if no key is configured: 'No API key found — set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or write ~/.config/wonderland/config.json.'

End-to-end acceptance test (live, gated behind WONDERLAND_LLM_SMOKE):
  - test_directive_to_live_watch_end_to_end: open NewRunScreen, fill in 'Build a /hello endpoint...' with smoke workflow + a tmp project root, press 'g', confirm, observe LiveRunScreen mount, drive the stream until RunEnded, assert artifacts on disk.
  - Skipped without WONDERLAND_LLM_SMOKE; expensive but the canonical proof point for the phase.

Acceptance: directive → live run → completion all from inside the TUI; first end-to-end completion of the operator interface vision.
tasks.resolution:
T53 closes P8.5. The whole loop is wired: directive composer → confirmation modal → Runner construction → LiveRunHandle → LiveRunScreen, all from inside the TUI.

Implementation:

  1. LiveRunScreen constructor extended to accept a pre-built RunHandle directly (in addition to snapshot_dir). When handle is provided, _consume_stream uses it; when only snapshot_dir is set, falls back to MockTurtleHandle as before. Same screen consumes live runs and replays interchangeably — UI code never branches on which it is.

  2. New screen src/wonderland/tui/screens/launch_confirmation.py with LaunchConfirmationScreen (ModalScreen). Shows directive preview + workflow + budget + project root, plus a 'this will burn API tokens' warning. Yes (y / Enter) returns True; No (n / Escape) returns False. The lazygit principle exception applies: irreversible actions get a guarded modal even though the rest of the UI is multi-pane. Burning \$3-5 qualifies.

  3. NewRunScreen.action_go full wire-up:
     - Validate inputs (existing)
     - Pre-flight API key check via env var > load_config (refuses to launch with a clear error rather than crashing on the first LLM call)
     - Save preset if checkbox is on (existing)
     - Stash launch params in self._pending_launch
     - Push LaunchConfirmationScreen with _on_launch_confirmed callback
     - Callback fires _launch_run worker on Yes; no-op on No

  4. _launch_run @work-decorated coroutine on NewRunScreen:
     - Loads workflow via load_workflow(name)
     - Constructs Runner via Runner.make_full_cast(project_root, budget_dollars)
     - Wraps in LiveRunHandle(runner, workflow, directive)
     - app.switch_screen(LiveRunScreen(handle=handle)) — swaps NewRunScreen for LiveRunScreen on the stack so escape from live-watch returns directly to the snapshot library, not back to the composer
     - Errors at any step surface as notifications without crashing

Tests (+4 in tests/test_tui_smoke.py):
  - launch_confirmation_dismisses_yes_no: Yes/No/Escape return correct boolean via push_screen callback
  - live_run_screen_accepts_handle_directly: passes a HistoricalRunHandle directly; v6 banner still shows 8 ribbon rows + accumulated cost
  - action_go_pushes_confirmation_modal: full form fill + Go pushes the LaunchConfirmationScreen on top
  - action_go_blocks_without_api_key: pre-flight refuses to launch when no key resolvable; stays on NewRunScreen

End-to-end live test: NOT shipped in T53 (would require WONDERLAND_LLM_SMOKE=1 + an API key + ~\$0.30 of API spend). The unit tests cover the wiring; user verification is the validation that matters here. Try 'wonderland-tui' → 'n' → pick 'ping' (cheapest preset) → Go → 'y' to confirm → watch the live screen render M1-M6 against a real Caucus bus. The pieces all pass tests; the integration point is right at the user's fingertips.

1391 tests pass full suite.

P8.5 closes — all five tasks done:
  T50 — Directive preset module + 5 bundled directives
  T51 — NewRunScreen layout (multi-pane, lazygit-shape, linear-form Enter advance)
  T52 — LiveRunHandle (RunnerEvent → RunEvent translation)
  T53 — Wire Go → live launch (this task)
  T54 — Save-as-preset (folded inline in T51)

The whole project becomes legible here. P8.4's live-watch screen consumes a real run streaming from a Caucus bus exactly the way it consumes a Mock Turtle replay. The directive issuer is a multi-pane composer with bundled + saved-per-project presets. The substrate the four prior tasks built makes T53's wire-up a few hundred lines instead of a structural overhaul.

Next: post-P8.5 PyPI release. Bump version to 0.1.0, update README, push to PyPI. Then P8.6 (new-project spinup) extends the on-ramp; P8.7 polishes the rough edges.

tasks.title: Save-as-preset — persist a custom directive to .wonderland/directives/
tasks.details:
Closes the preset loop with the per-project save story.

Trigger: 's' on NewRunScreen (or a button labeled 'Save as preset'). Opens a small modal:
  - Name: <text input> (slug, gets used for the YAML filename)
  - Title: <text input> (human-readable)
  - Description: <textarea> (paragraph)
  - Tags: <text input> (comma-separated)
  - [ ] Save with current workflow + skeleton as suggestions
  - Save / Cancel

The save target is project_root/.wonderland/directives/<slug>.yaml. If the project root isn't set, surface 'pick a project first' and route back to the project picker.

The new preset shows up in the preset picker on the left side of NewRunScreen immediately (refresh the list after save).

Tests:
  - Save a preset to a tmp project, verify the YAML file lands at the expected path
  - Re-list_project_directives picks it up
  - Re-load_directive against it round-trips the body correctly

Acceptance: from inside NewRunScreen, the user can type a directive, save it as a project preset, see it in the list, and re-select it on a future run without retyping.
tasks.resolution:
T54 (save-as-preset) folded into T51 follow-up per user feedback:

The original T54 plan was a separate modal screen for the save flow. User redirect after seeing T51's first cut: 'Also maybe a checkbox or something to save it as a new directive, will need an input for the preset name as well.' The inline shape is more lazygit-aligned (no modals except for irreversible actions), so the save form lives directly on NewRunScreen now:

  - Checkbox (id='save-checkbox', defaults off) on the config rows
  - Input (id='save-name-input') for the preset slug
  - 's' binding toggles the checkbox + focuses the name input
  - When the checkbox is on and Go is pressed, action_go saves the preset to project_root/.wonderland/directives/<name>.yaml before launching, then re-populates the preset table so the new entry appears immediately
  - Validation: empty name when checkbox is on → notification, no save attempted; project root must exist

Bonus convenience: when a preset is selected, save-name-input pre-fills with that preset's name (only when currently empty, so user-typed names aren't clobbered) — covers the natural 'edit-then-resave-as-new' flow with one fewer keystroke.

Test (tests/test_tui_smoke.py — test_new_run_screen_save_as_preset_persists_and_relists): fills the form, checks the save box, sets a name, calls action_go, asserts the YAML lands at the expected .wonderland/directives/ path AND the preset table re-populates with the new entry.

The original modal-based T54 design is superseded by this inline approach. Same outcome (per-project preset persistence) with less screen-pushing overhead.
